name: Avatar
purpose: Represents a person or entity as a small circular image or initials indicator — a table row, a nav footer, a comment author.
neverUseFor: Brand logomarks — use Image or a dedicated Logo component
Status indication — use StatusDot/Badge; Avatar communicates identity, not state
Large hero imagery — Avatar is capped at the field/control size scale, never a feature image
rationale: Avatar reuses the field scale's semantic.size.{s,m,l} rungs (24/32/40px) instead of a local scale, so it lines up with Inputs, table rows and nav footers without per-use tweaks. It is always a circle and carries identity only — never state — so the accessible name comes from alt/name exactly once and status stays the job of Badge/StatusDot.

mayExtendLocally: Supply any image source or initials fallback per product
Wrap an Avatar in a Tooltip or link at the usage site
mustEscalateToDS: Adding new sizes beyond s/m/l or non-circular shapes
Overlaying status indicators or borders onto the Avatar itself
Using Avatar for logos or hero imagery

anatomy.description: Fallback — the first letter of label, rendered when src is absent.

props.name: label
props.description: The person's full name — source for the initials fallback, and the accessible name (image alt / aria-label).

props.name: src
props.description: Image URL. When present, renders avatar-image; falls back to initials on load error.

props.name: size
props.description: Physical size. Shares the field scale with Input/Select (s=24, m=32, l=40).

height.note: Shares tokens with the Field scale (Input/Select) — same semantic.size.{s,m,l} rungs, not a new local scale.

width.note: Always a circle — width equals height at every size, no consumer override.

a11y.role: img (implicit via ) when src is set; presentation otherwise — the accessible name comes from the alt/name, never announced twice

properties.name: initials
properties.description: The first letter of `label` — code derives it, Figma takes it typed.

properties.name: src
properties.description: Shows avatar-image (an image fill covering the circle) over the initials — code renders one or the other. Swap the photo per instance with the image fill. The photo is one of the Pexels portraits in apps/storybook/public/avatars (flat-color backgrounds) — it lives only inside the component, not as loose images on the canvas.
